newsitem.title: UK: Bullion markets made a spectacular rebound.
newsitem.headline: Bullion markets made a spectacular rebound.

text.p: The price of gold staged a vigorous recovery from 3-3/4 year lows on Wednesday rising almost $10 an ounce in a less than an hour.
Dealers cited fund buying across the precious metals sector. Platinum was a favourite. Gold was lifted from an early $336.50 to as high as $345.50. Silver soared, too.
The dealers said buying led by the trade and hedge funds largely in New York turned round a market that had been extremely nervous.
"Everybody had the feeling there would be a big move today but until New York started the market was very nervous and most dealers were sitting with a square book," one insider said.
Technical analyst Cliff Green said, "Gold's decline to a landmark $340 level last Friday signalled a short lived but sharp corrective bounce which could take prices as high as $350."
By 1745 GMT gold was indicated at $345.55 per ounce and silver was 21 cents ahead of Tuesday at $5.14. But platinum took over leadership of the market with a rise of $14.00 on the day to $369.00.
"The funds have been playing the gold-platinum spread and that has really moved platinum" a dealer said.
He explained that the spread involved buying platinum and selling gold on the basis that the difference between the two metals would widen allowing a profit to be taken.
"It doesn't affect gold so much but it a small market like platinum, a spread play can send prices flying," he added.
Gold has been under pressure for weeks from threatened central bank sales. On January 13 the Dutch central bank said it had sold 300 tonnes of gold late in 1996.
Additional supply has poured into the market as gold producers also sold metal to protect their profit margins against declining prices.
The price fall has been accelerated recently by long term gold hoarders finally deciding that the high prices of the early 1980s were apparently gone for ever.
"The bank vaults get emptier and emptier every day," said one bullion dealer based in continental Europe.
The market's latest trauma came on Tuesday when the dollar surged to fresh 34-month highs against the mark and a near four-year high against the yen.
"The strong dollar put pressure on prices and caused a lot of selling late on Tuesday which continued on Wednesday. Further there were very few buyers around," a dealer said.
Dealers noted that a premium as wide as $21 for platinum over gold in a bear market was unusual.
Platinum usually took the limelight when economies were booming and the precious metals market were on an upswing, they said.
"Platinum had taken some of its strength for its sister metal palladium. Gold's underlying weakness is unrelated to the other precious metals," a dealer said.
Russia is the world's second largest supplier of platinum and largest exporter of palladium.

Its failure to open supply contract negotiations with its major customers including leading consumer Japan has lead to shortages of the metals and forced consumers to cover their needs in the dealer market.
"It is ironic that platinum surged on the day the Russian upper house finally approved the county's 1997 budget," a dealer said.

The supply talk were delayed partially due to the budget being undecided and also due to adminstrative problems after the previous preciousmetals export licensing committee was disbanded last last year.
"Platinum and palladium are fund led markets now," one dealer said.
